narrative: The model estimated your probability of bad credit at 27.0%, meaning it judged roughly a one-in-four chance of repayment difficulty. In this lending decision, that was above the risk cutoff, so your application was denied. The strongest reason was the size of the credit you requested: 11,054 DM, far above the average approved applicant’s request of about 3,020 DM. This was the top-ranked factor and pushed the decision toward bad credit. The next most important factor was your checking-account status, recorded as none, and the third was your savings information, recorded as unknown/none. Both ranked below loan size and, in your case, leaned toward good credit—they softened the risk picture but did not outweigh the concern created by the large amount. In practical terms, the requested loan was too large relative to the profile the lender associates with approval, even though your account and savings details were not additional negative drivers. To improve your chances, ask the lender what loan amount would be within an acceptable range and consider requesting substantially less. Provide clearer documentation of your checking and savings position if available, and ask whether a co-applicant or guarantor could strengthen a future application. Reapplying with a smaller request and more complete financial information is the most direct next step.
